claims.statement: Form N-400 is a sovereign onshore U.S. Citizenship / Naturalization application administered by USCIS, strictly classified as a non-visa status benefit (NOT a visa or consular entry clearance).
claims.legalInstrumentType: Non-Visa Citizenship / Naturalization Application
claims.issuingAuthority: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS — DHS)
claims.reviewerNotes: Phase 3.9.5 internal audit note (p2-cand-us-n400 S01): Verified against primary sovereign source.

claims.statement: Eligible applicants must already hold Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR / Green Card) status (or qualify through qualifying U.S. military service under INA §§ 328/329).
claims.legalInstrumentType: Non-Visa Citizenship / Naturalization Application
claims.issuingAuthority: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS — DHS)
claims.reviewerNotes: Phase 3.9.5 internal audit note (p2-cand-us-n400 S01): Verified against primary sovereign source.

claims.statement: Naturalization is never automatic or guaranteed; citizenship is conferred only after USCIS approval and administration of the Oath of Allegiance (INA § 337).
claims.legalInstrumentType: Non-Visa Citizenship / Naturalization Application
claims.issuingAuthority: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS — DHS)
claims.reviewerNotes: Phase 3.9.5 internal audit note (p2-cand-us-n400 S01): Verified against primary sovereign source.

claims.statement: Procedural filing rules are governed by Form N-400 instructions, INA § 334 (8 U.S.C. § 1445), and 8 CFR Part 334 under USCIS adjudication authority.
claims.legalInstrumentType: Non-Visa Citizenship / Naturalization Application
claims.issuingAuthority: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS — DHS)
claims.reviewerNotes: Phase 3.9.5 internal audit note (p2-cand-us-n400 S02): Verified against primary sovereign source.

claims.statement: Substantive statutory eligibility is governed separately by INA § 316 (8 U.S.C. § 1427, 5-year LPR rule) and 8 CFR Part 316.

claims.statement: Spousal naturalization (INA § 319(a), 8 U.S.C. § 1430) and English/civics examination mandates (INA § 312, 8 U.S.C. § 1423) operate as distinct statutory provisions.

claims.statement: General Track (INA § 316(a)): Applicant must be >=18 years old and an LPR for at least 5 years with >=30 months physical presence and >=3 months residence in the state/USCIS district.
claims.legalInstrumentType: Non-Visa Citizenship / Naturalization Application
claims.issuingAuthority: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS — DHS)

claims.statement: Spousal Track (INA § 319(a)): Applicant must be an LPR for at least 3 years living in marital union with a U.S. citizen spouse for 3 years, with >=18 months physical presence.

claims.statement: Principal Pass Holder Prerequisite: The principal sponsor must hold a valid Singapore Employment Pass (EP) or S Pass (Work Permit holders are ineligible; ONE Pass and EntrePass holders follow separate dependant criteria; overseas ICT EP holders under WTO GATS/FTA are ineligible unless covered by an applicable FTA).

claims.statement: NFQ Level 8 Award Duration: Graduates with an award at NFQ Level 8 are granted a 12-month Stamp 1G permission, subject to a maximum of 7 years' aggregate student/graduate permission overall (Stamp 2 + Stamp 1G).

claims.statement: NFQ Level 9 or Above Award Duration: Graduates with an award at NFQ Level 9 or above qualify for up to 24 months' Stamp 1G permission (granted initially for 12 months and renewable for an additional 12 months), subject to an overall limit of 8 years.
claims.legalInstrumentType: Post-Study Graduate Immigration Permission (Stamp 1G)

claims.issuingAuthority: Immigration Service Delivery (ISD), Department of Justice Ireland

claims.statement: Repeat-Use Limit: A graduate is not permitted to access the Third Level Graduate Programme on more than 2 separate occasions (e.g., once at Level 8 and once after achieving a Level 9+ award), subject to the 8-year overall cap.
